reason: Reference target types: the profile allows Reference(Practitioner) and the reference is Organization/o1. The Java validator checks target types only on references it can resolve; ours reads the type from the literal reference, as the profile requires.
openAtEnd slicing: R5 defines it as 'additional slices are allowed, but only at the end'. The Java validator (7.0.2) reports an unsliced value before a slice only as information; ours rejects it.
The example claims the core bodytemp profile, which is not in our active set, and violates it (no effective[x]): an error in HL7's example.
The example claims vhdir-location from the VhDir implementation guide, which is not in our active set.
Java policy, not an R5 conformance rule: example.org and example.com URLs are refused in some contexts.
Terminology: tier 4 (#90, #91). The differential runs the Java validator with terminology off; which of these it still reports depends on its terminology cache.
Resolution: the Java validator resolves canonical URLs and narrative links; our tiers do not dereference them.

Extensions without a definition in our active set are accepted (tier 3 checks the ones it has); the Java validator loads the HL7 extension packages and checks them. Depending on its environment, it also reads the R5 extended-contact-availability extension as allowing no types.
